headline: SDF Ends Its Independent Command
deck: Mazloum Abdi’s 25 August declaration folds the force into Syrian Army brigades under a single national chain. The communiqués leave the brigade map, commanders, payroll, weapons, detention sites, oil fields and crossings unpublished.
body: Mazloum Abdi announced on 25 August that the SDF’s mission had ended and the organisation would dissolve as an independent military force after integration into Syrian Army brigades [E1][E3]. The declared structure places those brigades under a single national chain of command [E1]. The same announcement says parallel military and administrative structures are ending [E1]. The dissolution announcement was reported at 10:14 p.m. local time, 19:14 UTC [E1].

Abdi framed the dissolution as the endpoint of a completed integration into Syrian Army brigades [E1][E3]. That conversion gives the top of the command chart a documented answer: one national military chain [E1]. The communiqués do not identify which former SDF element belongs to which brigade or through which named commander orders would flow [E1][E3]. They therefore publish the new command principle without publishing its subordinate roster [E1][E3].

President Ahmad al-Sharaa received Abdi and his delegation at the People’s Palace at 10:28 p.m. local time, 19:28 UTC [E2]. The declaration and palace meeting were reported fourteen minutes apart [E1][E2]. Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani and Deir Ezzor Governor Ziad al-Ayesh attended the meeting [E2]. The presidency said the talks covered integration into state institutions and next-phase steps [E2].

The 25 August communiqués name no formations, brigade numbers, commanders or unit roster [E1][E2][E3]. They print no payroll arrangements or disposition of heavy weapons [E1][E2][E3]. Detention sites, oil fields and border crossings are also absent from the published record [E1][E2][E3]. “Full integration” is therefore a communiqué-level status with no public roster showing the operational allocation beneath it [E1][E3].

Hawar News, an SDF-aligned outlet, carried the same institutional endpoint from the SDF side of the record [E3]. Its account described the end of the SDF’s mission, its dissolution and completion of integration into Syrian Army brigades [E3]. State and SDF-aligned reporting therefore converge on dissolution of the independent military organisation and absorption into army brigades [E1][E3]. Neither account supplies the missing unit-by-unit command ledger [E1][E3].

The official framing also reaches beyond uniformed command [E1][E2]. The dissolution announcement says parallel military and administrative structures are ending [E1]. The presidency says the evening meeting addressed integration into state institutions and the steps of the next phase [E2]. The published process therefore joins military absorption and institutional absorption under the same state-integration sequence [E1][E2].

The 25 August record changes the formal answer to who holds military command: one national chain and no independent SDF military organisation [E1][E3]. It gives no public ledger for the units, commanders, salaries, weapons or strategic sites through which that arrangement will operate [E1][E2][E3]. Abdi moved from announcing dissolution to a presidential meeting on integration and next-phase steps the same evening [E1][E2]. By night’s end, the independent command had an obituary; the brigades still had no public roster [E1][E2][E3].
